22271-schwartz-a-history-from-schwartz-b.creator: David Christie Murray
22271-schwartz-a-history-from-schwartz-b.description: A book by David Christie Murray. denly I became aware of a second presence in the chamber, and turned with an actual assurance that some one stood behind me. I was alone, as a single glance about the room informed me, but the sense of that second presence was so clearly defined and positive that the mere evidence of sight seemed doubtful.

Special Corrections for Over or Under Compensation. Example Illustrating that Temperature Variation  is Not Always Due to the Balance and Spring.

MANUSCRIPT FOUND IN A BOTTLE. THE MALAY PIRATE CHAPTER X. THE BADINAGE OF OLD FRIENDS. JOURNAL OF PAOLO LANGHETTI. THE SHADOW OF THE AFRICAN FOREST. BEATRICE’S JOURNAL CHAPTER XXV. arxiv-1906-08116.title: Search for Dilepton Resonances with the ATLAS Detector and Run 2 Data
arxiv-1906-08116.creator: Aaron White On behalf of the ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-1906-08116.description: Abstract A search for resonances in the dielectron and dimuon mass spectra from 250 GeV to 6 TeV is presented. The data were recorded during Run 2 of the LHC by the ATLAS experiment using proton-proton ( p ​ p pp ) collisions with a center-of-mass energy of s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV.

arxiv-2102-01792.title: A Survey on Understanding, Visualizations, and Explanation of Deep Neural Networks
arxiv-2102-01792.creator: Atefeh Shahroudnejad † {\dagger} Concordia Institute for Information Systems Engineering, Concordia University, Montreal, Canada
arxiv-2102-01792.description: Abstract Recent advancements in machine learning and signal processing domains have resulted in an extensive surge of interest in Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) due to their unprecedented performance and high accuracy for different and challenging problems of significant engineering importance.

arxiv-2105-06633.title: An algebra over the operad of posets and structural binomial identities
arxiv-2105-06633.creator: José Antonio Arciniega-Nevárez 1, Marko Berghoff 2, Eric Rubiel Dolores-Cuenca 3
arxiv-2105-06633.description: Abstract . We study generating functions of strict and non-strict order polynomials of series-parallel posets, called order series. These order series are closely related to Ehrhart series and h ∗ h^{*} -polynomials of the associated order polytopes. We explain how they can be understood as algebras over a certain operad of posets.

arxiv-2111-07387.title: Splitting integrators for stochastic Lie–Poisson systems
arxiv-2111-07387.creator: Charles-Edouard Bréhier, David Cohen, Tobias Jahnke
arxiv-2111-07387.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Charles-Edouard Bréhier, David Cohen, Tobias Jahnke. We study stochastic Poisson integrators for a class of stochastic Poisson systems driven by Stratonovich noise. Such geometric integrators preserve Casimir functions and the Poisson map property. For this purpose, we propose explicit stochastic Poisson integrators based on a splitting strategy, and analyse their qualitative and quantitative properties: preservation of Casimir functions, existence of almost sure or moment bounds, asymptotic preserving property, and strong and weak rates of convergence.

arxiv-2206-13756.title: On the Impact of Noises in Crowd-Sourced Data for Speech Translation
arxiv-2206-13756.creator: Siqi Ouyang, Rong Ye, Lei Li
arxiv-2206-13756.description: Abstract Training speech translation (ST) models requires large and high-quality datasets. MuST-C is one of the most widely used ST benchmark datasets. It contains around 400 hours of speech-transcript-translation data for each of the eight translation directions. This dataset passes several quality-control filters during creation.

arxiv-2211-02853.title: Self-Similar solution of rotating eruptive outflows on its equatorial plane Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2211-02853.creator: Takatoshi Ko, Kotaro Fujisawa, Toshikazu Shigeyama
arxiv-2211-02853.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Takatoshi Ko, Kotaro Fujisawa, Toshikazu Shigeyama. We construct axisymmetric self-similar solutions of transonic outflow s emanating from a point source including the effect of the rotation. The solutions are constructed exclusively on the equatorial plane. The features of solutions are determined by three parameters; the adiabatic index γ \gamma , the dimensionless coordinate of the transonic point, and the dimensionless azimuthal velocity at the transonic point. We classify the solutions into five groups according to the asymptotic behaviors.

arxiv-2302-04601.title: Magnetic square lattice with vertex coupling of a preferred orientation
arxiv-2302-04601.creator: Marzieh Baradaran, Pavel Exner, Jiří Lipovský
arxiv-2302-04601.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marzieh Baradaran, Pavel Exner, Jiří Lipovský. We analyze a square lattice graph in a magnetic field assuming that the vertex coupling is of a particular type violating the time reversal invariance. Calculating the spectrum numerically for rational values of the flux per plaquette we show how the two effects compete; at the high energies it is the magnetic field which dominates restoring asymptotically the familiar Hofstadter’s butterfly pattern.

arxiv-2308-07493.title: Neutrino charge radius and electromagnetic dipole moments via scalar and vector leptoquarks Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-2308-07493.creator: A. Bolaños–Carrera e1,addr1, M. Guiot–Lomelí e2,addr2, G. Tavares-Velasco e3,addr2
arxiv-2308-07493.description: Abstract The one-loop contribution of scalar and vector leptoquarks (LQs) to the electromagnetic properties (NEPs) of massive Dirac neutrinos is presented via an effective Lagrangian approach. For the contribution of gauge LQs to the effective neutrino charge radius defined in Bernabeu:2002nw , we considered a Yang-Mills scenario and used the background field method for the calculation.

arxiv-2404-00510.title: Denoising Low-dose Images Using Deep Learning of Time Series Images
arxiv-2404-00510.creator: Yang SHAO, Toshie YAGUCHI, Toshiaki TANIGAKI
arxiv-2404-00510.description: Abstract Digital image devices have been widely applied in many fields, including scientific imaging, recognition of individuals, and remote sensing. As the application of these imaging technologies to autonomous driving and measurement, image noise generated when observation cannot be performed with a sufficient dose has become a major problem.

arxiv-2407-09183.title: Search for neutral long-lived particles that decay into displaced jets in the ATLAS calorimeter in association with leptons or jets using p ​ p pp collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV
arxiv-2407-09183.creator: The ATLAS Collaboration
arxiv-2407-09183.description: Abstract A search for neutral long-lived particles (LLPs) decaying in the ATLAS hadronic calorimeter using 140 fb -1 of proton–proton collisions at s = 13 \sqrt{s}=13 TeV delivered by the LHC is presented. The analysis is composed of three channels.

arxiv-2408-09294.title: How to Make an Action Attractive Thanks: MP: Kelley School of Business, Indiana University, marpease@iu.edu & MW: Arizona State University, mark.whitmeyer@gmail.com . We thank Arjada Bardhi, Henrique Castro-Pires, Chris Chambers, Duarte Gonçalves, Faruk Gul, Ilia Krasikov, Pietro Ortoleva, and Sungm
arxiv-2408-09294.creator: Marilyn Pease and Mark Whitmeyer
arxiv-2408-09294.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marilyn Pease and Mark Whitmeyer. A policymaker often wants to steer a decision-maker toward one of two actions, but lacks reliable knowledge of how the decision-maker perceives uncertainty or evaluates risk. We formalize a notion of robust paternalism: a modification a ^ \hat{a} of a desired action a a is robustly more attractive than a a relative to b b if, for every belief over states and every increasing concave utility function, whenever the decision-maker prefers a a to b b , she also

arxiv-2411-04471.title: FQsun: A Configurable Wave Function-Based Quantum Emulator for Power-Efficient Quantum Simulations
arxiv-2411-04471.creator: TUAN HAI VU 1, VU TRUNG DUONG LE 1, HOAI LUAN PHAM 1, QUOC CHUONG NGUYEN 2, YASUHIKO NAKASHIMA 1
arxiv-2411-04471.description: Abstract Quantum computers are promising powerful computers for solving complex problems, but access to real quantum hardware remains limited due to high costs. Although the software simulators on CPUs/GPUs such as Qiskit, ProjectQ, and Qsun offer flexibility and support for many qubits, they struggle with high power consumption and limited processing speed, especially as qubit counts scale.

arxiv-2501-02857.title: ParetoLens: A Visual Analytics Framework for Exploring Solution Sets of Multi-objective Evolutionary Algorithms
arxiv-2501-02857.creator: Yuxin Ma, Zherui Zhang, Ran Cheng, Southern University of Science and Technology, China Yaochu Jin, Westlake University, China Kay Chen Tan, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong SAR, China
arxiv-2501-02857.description: Abstract In the domain of multi-objective optimization, evolutionary algorithms are distinguished by their capability to generate a diverse population of solutions that navigate the trade-offs inherent among competing objectives. This has catalyzed the ascension of evolutionary multi-objective optimization (EMO) as a prevalent approach. Despite the effectiveness of the EMO paradigm, the analysis of resultant solution sets presents considerable challenges.

arxiv-2502-10585.title: Prediction uncertainty-aware planning using deep ensembles and constrained trajectory optimisation
arxiv-2502-10585.creator: Anshul Nayak, Azim Eskandarian
arxiv-2502-10585.description: Abstract Human motion is stochastic and ensuring safe robot navigation in a pedestrian-rich environment requires proactive decision-making. Past research relied on incorporating deterministic future states of surrounding pedestrians which can be overconfident leading to unsafe robot behaviour. The current paper proposes a predictive uncertainty-aware planner that integrates neural network based probabilistic trajectory prediction into planning.

arxiv-2503-07023.title: On spaces of arc-smooth maps Thanks: This research was funded by the Austrian Science Fund (FWF) DOI 10.55776/PAT1381823. For open access purposes, the author has applied a CC BY public copyright license to any author-accepted manuscript version arising from this submission.
arxiv-2503-07023.creator: Armin Rainer
arxiv-2503-07023.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Armin Rainer. It is well-known that a function on an open set in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} is smooth if and only if it is arc-smooth, i.e., its composites with all smooth curves are smooth. In recent work, we extended this and related results (for instance a real analytic version) to suitable closed sets, notably, sets with Hölder boundary and fat subanalytic sets satisfying a necessary topological condition.

arxiv-2509-05430.title: Site Evaluation and Cost Estimation for Cosmic Explorer
arxiv-2509-05430.creator: Laurence Datrier, Geoffrey Lovelace, Joshua R. Smith, Andrew Saenz, Amber Romero, for the Cosmic Explorer Project
arxiv-2509-05430.description: Abstract Cosmic Explorer (CE) is a proposed next generation gravitational-wave observatory that would be sited in the United States. As of 2025, CE is in its design phase, with plans to begin operations in the 2030s together with the Einstein Telescope in Europe.

arxiv-2509-12092.title: Predicting Structural Relaxation in Supercooled Small Molecules via Molecular Dynamics Simulations and Microscopic Theory
arxiv-2509-12092.creator: Anh D. Phan, Ngo T. Que, Nguyen T. T. Duyen
arxiv-2509-12092.description: Abstract Understanding and predicting the glassy dynamics of small organic molecules is critical for applications ranging from pharmaceuticals to energy and food preservation. In this work, we present a theoretical framework that combines molecular dynamics simulations and Elastically Collective Nonlinear Langevin Equation (ECNLE) theory to predict the structural relaxation behavior of small organic glass-formers.

arxiv-2510-11486.title: 2-Factors in Graphs Thanks: The work leading to this paper was carried out at LSE, London, in 2011. Discussions with Monika Møbjerg Andersen at the University of Southern Denmark in the spring of 2011 are also acknowledged. The second author thanks the Danish Council for Independent Research (FNU) a
arxiv-2510-11486.creator: Jan van den Heuvel
arxiv-2510-11486.description: Abstract An account of 2 2 -factors in graphs and their history is presented. We give a direct graph-theoretic proof of the 2 2 -Factor Theorem and a new variant of it, and also a new complete characterisation of the maximal graphs without 2 2 -factors.

arxiv-2602-22705.title: Quantum Monte Carlo study of the metal-insulator crossover in the square-lattice Hubbard model
arxiv-2602-22705.creator: Mingzhong Lu, Yu-Feng Song, Youjin Deng, Yuan-Yao He
arxiv-2602-22705.description: Abstract The interaction-driven evolution from a Fermi liquid to a Mott insulator is a hallmark of strongly correlated fermion systems. In this work, we present a numerically unbiased study of such metal-to-insulator crossover in the half-filled square-lattice Hubbard model at finite temperatures, employing auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo method.

arxiv-2606-15101.title: Optimizing Wigner Negativity in Scattering Processes Using Energetic Cost Functions
arxiv-2606-15101.creator: Kian Hwee Lim, Kiarn T. Laverick, Sahil Sardar Jafar, Samyak P. Prasad, Maria Maffei, Alexia Auffèves

europmc-pmc6712367.title: Neurobiological links between stress and anxiety.
europmc-pmc6712367.creator: Daviu N, Bruchas MR, Moghaddam B, Sandi C, Beyeler A.
europmc-pmc6712367.description: Stress and anxiety have intertwined behavioral and neural underpinnings. These commonalities are critical for understanding each state, as well as their mutual interactions. Grasping the mechanisms underlying this bidirectional relationship will have major clinical implications...

pmc-10585648.title: Method of choosing soils as CEB or pavement layers based on geological and environmental information and mode of treatment✰
pmc-10585648.creator: Manefouet Kentsa Bertille Ilalie, Kamgang Kabeyene Beyala Véronique, Katte Yato Valentine, Wouatong Armand, Nzenti Jean Paul, Ndjigui Paul Désiré, Elimbi Antoine
pmc-10585648.description: During research on the geological, mineralogical, mechanical and geotechnical nature of thick layers of soils developed on the rocks of the lower zone of the southern slopes of Mount Bambouto (West Cameroon), a couple of observations were made. The mechanical behavior of soils as construction materials is linked to the nature of the parent rock and its environment of formation.

pmc-10611697.title: Anti-obesity effects of olivetol in adult zebrafish model induced by short-term high-fat diet
pmc-10611697.creator: Andukuri Reshma, T Tamilanban, V Chitra, Vetriselvan Subramaniyan, Gaurav Gupta, Neeraj Kumar Fuloria, Mahendran Sekar, Shivkanya Fuloria, Rakesh Sahu, J Narayanan, Srikumar Chakravarthy, Siddharthan Selvaraj
pmc-10611697.description: Obesity is a complex disease caused by various factors, and synthetic drugs used to treat it can have side effects. Natural compounds, such as olivetol, could be a promising alternative. Olivetol is a substance found in certain lichen species and has anti-inflammatory and anti-cancer properties.

pmc-10630124.title: A new Bayesian factor analysis method improves detection of genes and biological processes affected by perturbations in single-cell CRISPR screening
pmc-10630124.creator: Yifan Zhou, Kaixuan Luo, Lifan Liang, Mengjie Chen, Xin He
pmc-10630124.description: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) screening coupled with single-cell RNA sequencing has emerged as a powerful tool to characterize the effects of genetic perturbations on the whole transcriptome at a single-cell level. However, due to its sparsity and complex structure, analysis of single-cell CRISPR screening data is challenging.

pmc-11396474.title: No significant difference in salivary cortisol response on the Trier Social Stress Test-Online based on coffee consumption habits
pmc-11396474.creator: Masaharu Ueno
pmc-11396474.description: BackgroundCoffee is widely consumed around the world. In Japan, it is a type of “Shikohin” (consumed for flavor, not nutrition). Several medical studies have reported the beneficial effects of coffee consumption, whereas others suggest that these beneficial effects on psychological aspects are marginal.

pmc-11642656.title: Advances in the Mitigation of Microbiologically Influenced Concrete Corrosion: A Snapshot
pmc-11642656.creator: Husnu Gerengi, Ertugrul Kaya, Moses M Solomon, Matthew Snape, Andrea Koerdt, Ruiyong Zhang, Chao Liu, Yimeng Zhang
pmc-11642656.description: Concrete, a versatile construction material, faces pervasive deterioration due to microbiologically influenced corrosion (MIC) in various applications, including sewer systems, marine engineering, and buildings. MIC is initiated by microbial activities such as involving sulfate-reducing bacteria (SRB), sulfur-oxidizing bacteria (SOB), etc., producing corrosive substances like sulfuric acid. This process significantly impacts structures, causing economic losses and environmental concerns.

pmc-11669570.title: The JNK Signaling Pathway Regulates Seizures Through ENT1 in Pilocarpine‐Induced Epilepsy Rat Model
pmc-11669570.creator: Shun Liu, Zhong Luo, Fangjing Li, Lijia Zhang, Mingxiang Xie, Juan Yang, Zucai Xu
pmc-11669570.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveThe study investigates whether the expression and function of ENT1 can be regulated by inhibiting the JNK signaling pathway, thereby altering the levels of extracellular adenosine and glutamate in neurons, and subsequently affecting the progression of epilepsy.MethodsThe adult male SD rats were randomly divided into four groups: EP + SP600125 group, EP + DMSO group, EP group, and normal control group.

pmc-11691555.title: PREDICTORS OF CONTINUED ENGAGEMENT IN ONE’S FAVORITE ACTIVITY DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC
pmc-11691555.creator: Jeehoon Kim, Ji Hyun Lee
pmc-11691555.description: Active engagement is one of the important pillars in successful aging (Rowe & Kahn, 1997), however less is known about one’s favorite activity, a key source of enjoyment and meaning, in later life. In the context of higher constraints imposed during the pandemic, continuing one’s favorite activity can play a pivotal role in maintaining well-being for older adults.

pmc-12553379.title: Investigation of Exercise Status and Related Influencing Factors Among Maintenance Hemodialysis Patients in Nantong Region: A Cross-Sectional Study in China (2024–2025)
pmc-12553379.creator: Han Zhang, Ping Lu, Huijuan Shao, Juan Shan, Lin Hua, Ling Da
pmc-12553379.description: BackgroundThe physical activity level of Maintenance Hemodialysis (MHD) patients is closely associated with prognosis and quality of life. This study aimed to investigate the exercise status and influencing factors among MHD patients in the Nantong region.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted among 227 MHD patients from three hospitals in Nantong, China, between June 2024 and February 2025.

pmc-12651484.title: Impact of a nudge-based intervention on hand soap usage in a Japanese Hospital: interrupted time series analysis
pmc-12651484.creator: Tetsuji Morishita, Masayoshi Monji, Masao Kuwabara, Shin Lee, Makoto Hayashi, Hisashi Tsurumi, Hidetoshi Matsunami
pmc-12651484.description: SummaryBackgroundThis study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of nudge-based messages on hand soap usage in a Japanese hospital setting.MethodsInterrupted time series analysis was conducted using monthly hand soap usage data from April 2022 to March 2024. The following nudge messages were placed in restrooms: “Are your neighbors washing their hands with soap?” (men) and “Water does not disinfect; soap works!

pmc-12860172.title: The effect of melanocortin-4 receptor agonist drugs on obesity and metabolic risk factors: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-12860172.creator: Yanan Sun, Mohammad Abed, Mohammad Hassan Sohouli
pmc-12860172.description: BackgroundThe melanocortin-4 receptor (MC4R) agonists have emerged as potential treatments for obesity, particularly in patients with rare genetic syndromes. However, their overall effects on obesity and cardiometabolic risk factors remain uncertain. To systematically evaluate the efficacy of MC4R agonists on weight-related outcomes and cardiometabolic risk factors.MethodsWe conducted this study following PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

pmc-13270398.title: When can AlphaFold predict the oligomeric states of proteins?
pmc-13270398.creator: Yiechang Lin, Ciara Wallis, Ben Corry
pmc-13270398.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Homooligomerisation is a prevalent and important process that many proteins undergo to form the quaternary structures required for biological function. However, determining oligomeric states and structures experimentally remains technically challenging and time‐consuming for many proteins. Here, we show that the protein structure prediction tools AlphaFold2‐Multimer and AlphaFold3 can be used to quickly and accurately predict oligomeric states and structures for a range of soluble and membrane proteins.

pmc-13283921.title: Diagnosing Syndrome‐Like Microangiopathic Hemolytic Anemia After Pit Viper Envenomation: Overcoming Laboratory Gaps in a Resource‐Limited Setting: A Case Report From Nepal

pmc-13389205.title: SHAP analysis of an improved EEG-based mental workload classification framework: utilizing data augmentation and explainable AI
pmc-13389205.creator: Sushil Chaturvedi, Mitul Kumar Ahirwal
pmc-13389205.description: Mental workload (MWL) classification using electroencephalogram (EEG) signals is crucial for cognitive neuroscience and is also a challenging research area in brain-computer interface (BCI). Since the EEG signals fluctuate a lot across sessions and individuals, there is a need for a robust classification model that generalizes well for real-world applications.

pmc-13678992.title: Derived inflammatory indicators for identifying preeclampsia in pregnant patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: a case–control study
pmc-13678992.creator: Jiaxin Huo, Minyi Zhang, Haoyue Hu, Yinghua Xu, Shujie Liu, Jun Chen, Jiayi Zhou, Sishi Song, Manna Sun, Guifang Hu, Mei Zhong
pmc-13678992.description: BackgroundPregnant women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) are at high risk of preeclampsia (PE). However, overlapping clinical features between the two conditions make it challenging to detect superimposed PE. Failure to promptly recognize PE significantly increases the risk of adverse pregnancy outcomes. In recent years, complete blood count–derived inflammatory indicators (e.g.
